definition_zh: 组；群；团体；集团；（动词）把……分组；归类
definition_en: a number of people or things that are placed or considered together; to put people or things into such a set
core_image: 几个人肩并肩围成一个圈：单独的人聚在一起就成了一个整体
scene: 英语课上新来的老师让大家自由组合完成项目，同学们很快各自围成了小圈子。The students formed a group to work on the science project.
sceneCN: 这里 group 是「小组、团体」（第 1 个义项：因共同目的聚在一起的人）；句意是学生们组成小组来做科学项目。

derivatives.zh: 由 group 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「分组；归类」
由 re-（重新）+ group 构成，义为「重新集结；重组」

senses.title: A set of people together
senses.definition: several people who are together or connected in some way
senses.definitionCN: 因共同目的、关系或位置聚在一起的一些人
senses.example: A group of tourists gathered outside the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 一群游客聚集在博物馆外面。
senses.why: The core image is people standing shoulder to shoulder, so the human crowd sense grows straight out of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是人们肩并肩围在一起，所以「一群人」这个义项最贴近画面本身。

senses.title: A set of things of the same kind
senses.definition: several things that belong or are placed together
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起或属于同类的几样东西
senses.example: She put the keys in the group of small metal objects on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钥匙放进桌上那堆小金属物件里。
senses.why: When the image no longer needs people, any collection of similar items can fill the same circle shape.
senses.whyCN: 当画面里不再需要人时，任何同类物品都能填进同一个圈，于是延伸出「一组物品」。

senses.title: An organization or company
senses.definition: a number of companies or organizations controlled in a similar way
senses.definitionCN: 由同一家管理或控制的若干公司或组织
senses.example: The media group owns three newspapers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家传媒集团拥有三家报纸。
senses.why: A company made of many parts is itself a crowd of smaller units, so the crowd image extends to business.
senses.whyCN: 企业由许多小单位聚成，本质还是「聚成一团」，画面延伸到商业领域就成了「集团」。

senses.title: A category for sorting
senses.definition: a set into which things are divided for study or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为研究或整理而划分出的一类
senses.example: Divide the animals into groups by size.
senses.exampleCN: 按体型把这些动物分成几类。
senses.why: Drawing a circle around similar things is exactly how people classify, so the picture becomes a sorting tool.
senses.whyCN: 在同类东西外面画个圈，这正是分类的动作，画面自然变成了分类工具。

senses.title: To put into sets
senses.definition: to place people or things together because they share a feature
senses.definitionCN: 把有共同点的人或物聚在一起放置或整理
senses.example: The teacher grouped the pupils by reading level.
senses.exampleCN: 老师按阅读水平给学生分组。
senses.why: Once the circle exists as an idea, drawing it becomes an action, so the noun turns into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 「圈」这个概念一旦确立，画圈就成了动作，名词顺理成章转成动词。

intro.en: The word group entered English relatively late and carries the idea of a drawn cluster.
intro.cn: group 进入英语的时间相对较晚，一直保留着「聚成一团」的画面。

items.en: Italian gruppo meant a knot or cluster, used by artists for a cluster of figures in a painting.
items.cn: 意大利语 gruppo 指结块、一簇，画家用它指画中聚在一起的一组人物。

items.en: The Italian word itself is often traced to Germanic grondo related to the root of grunt, though this is disputed.
items.cn: 意大利语这个词一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语 grondo，与 grunt（咕哝）的词根有关，但此说存疑。

items.en: English borrowed gruppo as group around the late seventeenth century, first for clusters of figures in art.
items.cn: 约十七世纪末英语借入 gruppo，拼作 group，最初用于艺术作品中的人物群像。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the meaning widened to any collection of people or things.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义扩大到任何聚在一起的人或物。

items.en: Modern usage added the verb sense and the business sense of a group of companies.
items.cn: 现代用法又增加了动词义和「企业集团」义。

note.en: These words are close in form or meaning to group.
note.cn: 这些词在词形或词义上与 group 相近。

entries.definition: a small round fruit growing in clusters on vines
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄，成串长在藤上；与 group 只是拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: to feel about with the hands uncertainly
entries.definitionCN: 摸索；与 group 拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a large game bird; also to complain
entries.definitionCN: 松鸡；也指抱怨；形近但词源不同

entries.definition: a tight group of similar things growing or held together
entries.definitionCN: 一簇；一群，强调密集聚在一起

entries.definition: a large number of people gathered together
entries.definitionCN: 人群，规模较大且较杂

entries.definition: a group of people doing something together
entries.definitionCN: 一伙；一队，常指为一事联合的人

normalIntro.en: Five practical memory hooks for group.
normalIntro.cn: 五条关于 group 的实用记忆钩子。

normal.en: gr + oup: think of a group standing in a circle
normal.cn: gr + oup：想象一群人围成一圈，正是「组」的画面。

normal.en: grape grows in a group on the vine
normal.cn: 葡萄在藤上成串聚生，grape 和 group 都来自聚集的画面。

normal.en: in groups of four is a fixed classroom phrase
normal.cn: in groups of four（四人一组）是课堂固定表达，背下来即会用。

normal.en: group work means working together, not alone
normal.cn: group work 即小组合作，词义和场景绑定记忆。

normal.en: the verb group things means to sort them into circles
normal.cn: 动词 group things 就是把东西「圈」进不同类别。

abstract.en: one circle drawn around many dots
abstract.cn: 在许多圆点外画一个圈，圈住的就是一个 group。

abstract.en: shoulders touching, one unit
abstract.cn: 肩并肩挤在一起，散点变成一个整体。

abstract.en: many hands, one task
abstract.cn: 许多只手做同一件事，就是团队。

examples.en: The class split into three groups for the quiz.
examples.cn: 全班为测验分成了三个小组。

examples.en: Group the cards by color before you start.
examples.cn: 开始前先把卡片按颜色分组。

examples.en: A small group of villagers repaired the bridge.
examples.cn: 一小群村民修好了那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「孤扑」——一个人孤单地扑向人群，终于加入了一个 group（小组）。

root: 一般认为来自意大利语 gruppo（一簇、结块），可能进一步追溯到日耳曼语与 grunt（咕哝）相关的词根，此说存疑；核心画面是「聚成一团」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a crowd of people to any collection, then to organizations and sorting, and finally to the verb of drawing circles.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「一群人」扩展到「一组物品」，再到「机构、类别」，最后发展出「分组」的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many units inside one circle
core.cn: 核心意象：许多单位被同一个圈圈住

intro.en: Group is a short root with few built-in parts, so this section looks at nearby shapes instead.
intro.cn: group 本身极短，没有内部词缀，这一栏改为观察与它形近或相关的构词部件。

latinIntro.en: Latin-based neighbors that often appear beside group in school texts.
latinIntro.cn: 校园文本中常与 group 同现的拉丁语系近形词。

items.example: The team regrouped after the loss.
The grouping of the data took hours.
items.exampleCN: 给数据分组花了好几个小时。

items.example: There are five groups in the class.
A grape looks like it belongs in a group.
items.exampleCN: 一颗葡萄看上去就像属于一串。

items.example: A crowd is a big, loose group.

definition_zh: 生长；长大；种植；变得；逐渐变成
definition_en: to develop and become larger or taller; to plant and care for something so it develops; to gradually become
core_image: 一粒种子从土里探出头，慢慢拔高，最后长成大树
scene: 奶奶在院子里埋下桃核，每天浇水，看着小苗一点点升高。The little tree will grow quickly if you water it every day.
sceneCN: 这里 grow 是「生长、长高」（第 1 个义项：生物自然变大）；句意是每天浇水小树就会长得很快。

derivatives.zh: 由 grow 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「生长；增长」
由 grow 加 -er 构成，义为「种植者；栽培者」

senses.title: To develop in size naturally
senses.definition: to get bigger or taller as part of natural development
senses.definitionCN: 作为自然发育过程而变大变高
senses.example: Children grow fast in their first years.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在最初几年长得很快。
senses.why: The picture is a seed pushing upward, so the first sense is simply natural increase.
senses.whyCN: 画面是种子向上顶出土壤，第一个义项就是最直观的自然增大。

senses.title: To plant and raise crops
senses.definition: to put plants in soil and help them develop
senses.definitionCN: 把植物种进土里并帮它发育
senses.example: Farmers here grow vegetables all year round.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民全年种植蔬菜。
senses.why: If you help a plant grow, we say you grow it; the helper borrows the plant's verb.
senses.whyCN: 帮植物长大就说「种植」，帮助者借用了植物的动词。

senses.title: To become gradually
senses.definition: to slowly change into a state or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地进入某种状态或情绪
senses.example: The room grew quiet as the film began.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开场时房间渐渐安静下来。
senses.why: Getting taller happens slowly, so the same slow slide describes changes of feeling or state.
senses.whyCN: 长高是缓慢的过程，这种缓慢的变化同样可以描述状态或情绪的改变。

senses.title: To increase in amount
senses.definition: to become larger in number, amount, or strength
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、规模或力量上变大
senses.example: The city has grown quickly in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间这座城市扩张得很快。
senses.why: Anything that swells like a plant is described with the same upward image.
senses.whyCN: 任何像植物一样膨胀壮大的事物，都借用同一幅向上的画面。

senses.title: To let hair or nails lengthen
senses.definition: to stop cutting so that hair or nails become longer
senses.definitionCN: 停止修剪使头发或指甲变长
senses.example: He is growing a beard for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他冬天打算留胡子。
senses.why: Hair grows by itself; letting it happen makes you the owner of the process.
senses.whyCN: 头发会自己长，任其生长就让养发者成了这一过程的主导者。

intro.en: Grow is a pure Germanic word with a very old farming root.
intro.cn: grow 是纯粹的日耳曼语词，词根古老，与农耕生活相关。

items.en: Old Norse groja meant to green or sprout, related to the green of new plants.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 groja 意为发绿、发芽，与嫩苗的绿色相关。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic root gro- connects growing things with green color.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根 gro- 把「生长之物」与「绿色」联系在一起。

items.en: Old English growan meant to grow, increase, or develop, already used for people, plants, and numbers.
items.cn: 古英语 growan 意为生长、增长、发育，已可用于人、植物和数量。

items.en: Middle English kept the word and added the farming sense of growing crops.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用该词，并增加了种植庄稼的农事义。

items.en: Modern English completed the picture with the linking-verb sense of gradually becoming.
items.cn: 现代英语补全画面，增加了「渐渐变得」的系动词用法。

note.en: Words shaped like grow or close to it in meaning.
note.cn: 与 grow 词形相近或词义相关的词。

entries.definition: a large black bird
entries.definitionCN: 乌鸦；与 grow 只是拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: to give out a soft light
entries.definitionCN: 发光；与 grow 形近但词源不同

entries.definition: the past participle of grow, meaning fully developed
entries.definitionCN: grow 的过去分词，义为「成熟的；长大的」

entries.definition: to move upward or increase
entries.definitionCN: 上升；增长，强调动作方向

entries.definition: to grow or change into a bigger or better form
entries.definitionCN: 发展；发育，强调过程变化

entries.definition: to begin to grow, as a bud or shoot
entries.definitionCN: 发芽；抽枝，强调生长的开始

normalIntro.cn: 五条 grow 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: grew and grown are the two irregular past forms
normal.cn: grew 和 grown 是两个不规则过去形式，一起背。

normal.en: grow up means becoming an adult, grow old means aging
normal.cn: grow up 长大成人，grow old 变老，两句对照记忆。

normal.en: grow and green share the old root of living plants
normal.cn: grow 与 green 同源于有生命植物的老词根。

normal.en: farmers grow crops, gardeners grow flowers
normal.cn: 农民种庄稼、园丁种花，用场景固定动词义。

normal.en: grow tired, grow quiet, grow dark all mean gradually become
normal.cn: grow tired / quiet / dark 都是「渐渐变得」。

abstract.en: a sprout pushing out of dark soil
abstract.cn: 嫩芽顶破黑土，向上生长的画面。

abstract.en: a ruler line climbing year by year
abstract.cn: 身高尺上的刻度逐年上移。

abstract.en: a shadow lengthening as evening comes
abstract.cn: 傍晚影子慢慢拉长，事物渐渐变化。

examples.en: Tomatoes grow best in warm sunny places.
examples.cn: 西红柿在温暖向阳的地方长得最好。

examples.en: She grew more confident after the speech.
examples.cn: 演讲之后她变得更有自信了。

examples.en: My little brother has grown out of his shoes.
examples.cn: 我弟弟长得已经穿不下原来那双鞋了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「割肉」——庄稼割了一茬又长一茬，grow（生长）就是不停往上蹿。

root: 来自古英语 growan，可追溯至原始日耳曼语词根 gro-（生长、变绿），与古诺斯语 groja 同源；核心画面是植物由绿芽开始向上生长。

sensesIntro.en: From natural increase the word extends to farming, gradual change, numeric growth, and even hair.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「自然生长」扩展到「种植」「渐渐变得」「数量增长」，甚至「留发」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed pushing upward
core.cn: 核心意象：种子向上顶出土壤

intro.en: Grow itself has no prefix or suffix, so these items show how small endings build words from it.
intro.cn: grow 本身无前后缀，这一栏展示由它衍生构词的常用部件。

latinIntro.en: Latin-based endings that attach to English verbs like grow.
latinIntro.cn: 可附着于 grow 这类英语动词的拉丁语系词尾。

items.example: A rose grower opened a shop.
items.exampleCN: 一位玫瑰种植者开了店。
正在生长的嫩芽需要水。

items.example: He grew out of those clothes.
items.exampleCN: 他长得穿不下那些衣服了。

items.example: They raise chickens, not grow them.

definition_zh: 保卫；看守；防护；警惕；卫兵；防护装置
definition_en: to keep someone or something safe from danger or attack; a person or thing that protects
core_image: 一名卫兵笔直站在大门前，双手如盾挡在危险与门之间
scene: 博物馆展厅入口站着一位站姿笔挺的工作人员，提醒大家不要触碰展柜。The guard stopped the visitors from touching the glass case.
sceneCN: 这里 guard 是「警卫、看守者」（第 3 个义项：负责保护的人）；句意是警卫阻止游客触碰玻璃展柜。

pos.zh: 卫兵；警卫；防护装置；警惕

derivatives.zh: 由 guard 加名词后缀构成，义为「监护人；守护者」
由 guard + house 构成，义为「卫兵室」
由 guard + rail 构成，义为「护栏」
由 guard 加 -ed 构成，义为「谨慎的；有所保留的」
由 van-（在前）+ guard 构成，义为「先锋；前哨」

senses.title: To protect from danger
senses.definition: to keep a person or place safe from harm
senses.definitionCN: 使人或地方免受伤害
senses.example: Dogs guard the farm at night.
senses.exampleCN: 狗在夜里看守农场。
senses.why: The image is a shield standing between danger and what is protected, so the verb means blocking harm.
senses.whyCN: 画面是挡在危险与保护对象之间的盾，动词义就是拦截伤害。

senses.title: To watch carefully
senses.definition: to watch a person or place to stop escape or theft
senses.definitionCN: 看住人或地方以防逃跑或偷窃
senses.example: Two officers guard the prison gate.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警官看守监狱大门。
senses.why: A shield must also have eyes; standing watch is the watching half of protecting.
senses.whyCN: 盾还要有眼睛，站岗放哨就是「保护」里看的部分。

senses.title: A person who protects
senses.definition: a person whose job is to protect a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 以保护某地或某人为职责的人
senses.example: The bank guard opened the door for us.
senses.exampleCN: 银行保安为我们开了门。
senses.why: The doer of the action becomes the name of the person, as often happens in English.
senses.whyCN: 执行动作的人顺理成章变成名词，英语里常见这种转变。

senses.title: A device that protects
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that covers a dangerous part of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 盖住机器危险部位的装置
senses.example: Always use the blade guard on the saw.
senses.exampleCN: 用锯子时务必装上锯片护罩。
senses.why: If a person can guard, a barrier can too; the shield image turns into hardware.
senses.whyCN: 人能守卫，屏障也能，盾的画面变成了实物装置。

senses.title: Careful attention to prevent mistakes
senses.definition: care taken to avoid a mistake or danger
senses.definitionCN: 为避免错误或危险而保持的小心
senses.example: Keep guard against careless spelling in exams.
senses.exampleCN: 考试要防范粗心的拼写错误。
senses.why: Protection begins in the mind; staying alert is protecting before danger arrives.
senses.whyCN: 保护始于内心，警惕就是在危险到来之前先行设防。

intro.en: Guard came into English through French from a Germanic root about watching over.
intro.cn: guard 经法语进入英语，源自日耳曼语词根，意为「看护」。

items.en: A West Germanic root wardon meant to watch over and protect.
items.cn: 西日耳曼语词根 wardon 意为看护、保护。

items.en: Old French garder meant to keep, watch, and protect, borrowing the Germanic root.
items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为保存、看守、保护，借用了日耳曼词根。

items.en: Old Norse vartha, from the same Germanic stock, gave English the close relative ward.
items.cn: 同一日耳曼语系的古诺斯语 vartha 给英语带来近亲 ward。

items.en: Middle English took guard from Old French in the fourteenth century for soldiers watching a place.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语从古法语借入 guard，指看守之地的士兵。

items.en: Modern English kept both the person and the device senses and added guard against for caution.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「人」与「装置」两义，并增加 guard against 表防范。

note.en: Words close to guard in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guard 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: to guard; a person under protection
entries.definitionCN: 看守；受监护人；与 guard 同源，经不同路径进入英语

entries.definition: a promise that something will be done or given
entries.definitionCN: 保证；担保；与 guard 同出一源

entries.definition: one who guards, especially a child's legal protector
entries.definitionCN: 守护者；尤指未成年人的法定监护人

entries.definition: to protect against attack
entries.definitionCN: 防御；保卫，强调抵抗进攻

entries.definition: to keep safe from harm
entries.definitionCN: 保护，强调使之安全

entries.definition: to look at carefully for danger
entries.definitionCN: 看守；监视，强调观察

normalIntro.cn: 五条 guard 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: guard and ward are twins from one Germanic root
normal.cn: guard 与 ward 同源，是日耳曼词根的双胞胎。

normal.en: guarantee keeps the same family shape gu- + ar
normal.cn: guarantee 保留同族 gu- + ar 的字形，联想记忆。

normal.en: security guard is the fixed job title
normal.cn: security guard（保安）是固定职业名称，见得多就记得牢。

normal.en: off guard means unprepared, like a shield down
normal.cn: off guard（措手不及）就像盾放下了。

normal.en: guard against + danger is the standard warning pattern
normal.cn: guard against + 危险是标准警示搭配。

abstract.en: a straight figure blocking a doorway
abstract.cn: 一个人笔直堵在门口，成为活盾。

abstract.en: eyes sweeping left and right
abstract.cn: 双眼左右扫视，寸步不离。

abstract.en: a metal cover over sharp blades
abstract.cn: 利刃之上罩一块金属护罩。

examples.en: The goal keeper guarded the net skillfully.
examples.cn: 守门员出色地守住了球门。

examples.en: Wear gloves to guard your hands from the cold.

examples.en: His calm reply caught the reporter off guard.
examples.cn: 他平静的回答让记者措手不及。

sensesIntro.en: From protecting people and places the word moves to watchers, devices, and mental alertness.
sensesIntro.cn: 从保护人与地方，扩展到看守者、防护装置，再到心理上的警惕。

definition_zh: 猜测；推测；猜中；猜想；估计
definition_en: to give an answer or opinion without being sure of the facts; to find an answer by chance
core_image: 一个人皱眉盯着谜题，手指悬在两个选项之间犹豫不决
scene: 猜灯谜的摊位前排着长队，小华盯着灯笼上的谜面想了半天。She made a guess and wrote down three little lantern riddles answers.
sceneCN: 这里 guess 是「猜、推测」（第 1 个义项：不确定时给出答案）；句意是她凭猜测写下了三个灯谜的答案。

derivatives.zh: 由 guess 加 -er 构成，义为「猜测者」
由 guess 加 -ed 构成，义为「猜出的；凭猜测得到的」

senses.title: To answer without certainty
senses.definition: to give an answer when you are not sure it is right
senses.definitionCN: 在不确定答案是否正确时给出回答
senses.example: Guess how many sweets are in the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 猜猜罐子里有多少颗糖。
senses.why: The image is a hand hovering between choices, so the first sense is choosing without proof.
senses.whyCN: 画面是手指在选项间悬停，第一个义项就是没有把握时做出选择。

senses.title: To find correctly by chance
senses.definition: to reach the right answer even without knowing the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在不了解实情的情况下碰巧得出正确答案
senses.example: You guessed the ending of the film exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 你把电影结局猜得一模一样。
senses.why: A hovering hand sometimes lands on truth; luck turns a guess into a hit.
senses.whyCN: 悬停的手偶尔会落在正确答案上，运气让猜测变成了猜中。

senses.title: To suppose or believe
senses.definition: to think or believe something in a mild way, as in I guess
senses.definitionCN: 委婉地认为或相信，如 I guess 的用法
senses.example: I guess you are tired after the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 我想旅途之后你累了吧。
senses.why: Weak certainty sounds like an inner guess, so the verb softens into polite supposing.
senses.whyCN: 把握不大的想法听起来像心里的猜测，动词因此弱化为委婉的「我想」。

senses.title: To estimate a number or amount
senses.definition: to judge a number, size, or amount roughly
senses.definitionCN: 对数字、大小或数量作粗略判断
senses.example: Can you guess the weight of this box?
senses.exampleCN: 你能估计这个箱子的重量吗？
senses.why: Numbers hide behind facts, so rough answers about them are guesses too.
senses.whyCN: 数字藏在事实背后，对它们的粗略回答同样属于猜测。

senses.title: A try with uncertain result
senses.definition: an answer or opinion given without certainty
senses.definitionCN: 不确定之下给出的答案或看法
senses.example: That was only a guess, not the real answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个猜测，不是真正的答案。
senses.why: The action freezes into a noun when we talk about the answer itself rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 当我们谈论答案本身而非动作时，动作就凝固成名词。

intro.en: Guess has a Scandinavian-shaped history and always meant choosing in the dark.
intro.cn: guess 的历史带有斯堪的纳维亚色彩，一直表示在不明中做出选择。

items.en: Middle Dutch and Old English forms like gessen suggest a North Sea Germanic word about trying or getting.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语与古英语的 gessen 等形式显示这是北海日耳曼语词，意为尝试、获取。

items.en: The exact root is uncertain, though the sense of hitting upon something is stable across theories.
items.cn: 确切词根存疑，但各假说中「碰巧得到」的核心含义是一致的。

items.en: Middle English gessen meant to aim, estimate, or hit upon, first recorded in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 gessen 意为瞄准、估计、碰巧得到，最早见于十三世纪。

items.en: The spelling with -u- spread by analogy with guest and guard words from French.
items.cn: 带 -u- 的拼写受 guest、guard 等法语借词类推影响而普及。

items.en: Modern English settled the senses of supposing, estimating, and hitting the right answer.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了「猜想」「估计」「猜中」三个核心义项。

note.en: Words near guess in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guess 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: an outward appearance, often hiding the truth

entries.definition: to think something is likely true

entries.definition: to judge an amount roughly
entries.definitionCN: 估算，侧重数量判断

entries.definition: to take something as true before proof
entries.definitionCN: 假定；想当然，未证先认

normal.cn: guess 与 guest 只差最后一个字母，对照记忆防混淆。

normal.cn: I guess 是 I think 的委婉说法，口语高频。

normal.en: Guess what starts an exciting story
normal.cn: Guess what（你猜怎么着）常用来开头讲趣事。

normal.en: a wild guess means almost pure luck
normal.cn: a wild guess（瞎猜）几乎全凭运气。

normal.en: guessing games train the verb best
normal.cn: 玩猜谜游戏最能记住这个动词。

abstract.en: a hand hovering over two doors
abstract.cn: 一只手悬在两扇门之间，不知推哪扇。

abstract.en: a coin spinning before it lands
abstract.cn: 硬币旋转未落，答案未定。

abstract.en: eyes squeezed shut while pointing
abstract.cn: 闭着眼伸手指，赌一个结果。

examples.en: I guess the party starts at seven.
examples.cn: 我猜聚会七点开始。

examples.en: Her first guess about the puzzle was right.
examples.cn: 她对谜题的第一次猜测就是对的。

examples.en: Do not guess on the test; read the question twice.
examples.cn: 考试别乱猜，把题目读两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎死」——猜不中急得嘎嘎叫，guess（猜）就是要大胆开口。

root: 一般认为源自北海日耳曼语，与中古荷兰语 gessen、古英语 gessen（瞄准、碰巧得到）同源；确切词根存疑，核心含义是「在不明中碰运气」。

sensesIntro.en: From answering blindly the word widens to lucky hits, soft opinions, estimates, and finally the noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「瞎猜」扩展到「猜中」「委婉的认为」「估算」，最后凝固为名词。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手悬在两个答案之间

intro.cn: guess 是光杆动词，下面列出其词尾与近缘词。

latinIntro.cn: guess 的近亲多来自日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.example: A lucky guesser won the prize.
The guest arrived, not the guess.

definition_zh: 客人；宾客；旅客；特邀嘉宾
definition_en: a person who is received or entertained in another's home, hotel, or show
core_image: 一位客人推开主人家的门，主人笑着递上一杯热茶
scene: 周末外婆家来了几位远道而来的亲戚，客厅里摆满了水果和茶点。Every guest was offered a cup of hot tea at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 guest 是「客人、宾客」（第 1 个义项：受主人接待的人）；句意是每位客人一进门就获赠一杯热茶。

pos.zh: 客人；宾客；旅客；特邀嘉宾

derivatives.zh: 由 guest + house 构成，义为「宾馆；招待所」
与 guest 相对的女主人（提示对照记忆），义为「女主人」
与 guest 同源（古英语 gast），义为「幽灵」，词形相近

senses.title: A visitor at a home
senses.definition: someone welcomed into another person's house
senses.definitionCN: 被主人欢迎进家门的人
senses.example: We invited ten guests to dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们邀请了十位客人来吃饭。
senses.why: The core picture is a door opened by a host, so the first sense is the welcomed visitor.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是主人打开的门，第一个义项就是受欢迎的来访者。

senses.title: A paying customer at a hotel
senses.definition: a person staying at a hotel or guesthouse
senses.definitionCN: 住在旅馆或招待所里的人
senses.example: The hotel has two hundred guests tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆今晚住着两百位客人。
senses.why: A hotel acts as a giant host, so its customers are honored as guests.
senses.whyCN: 旅馆扮演大主人，房客于是被尊称为 guest。

senses.title: An invited person on a show
senses.definition: a person invited to appear on a program or at an event
senses.definitionCN: 应邀出现在节目或活动上的人
senses.example: Tonight's guest is a famous singer.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚的嘉宾是一位著名歌手。
senses.why: The show invites you in like a house does; being invited keeps the same image.
senses.whyCN: 节目像家庭一样发出邀请，受邀感让画面保持一致。

senses.title: Anything received free for a while
senses.definition: something given a temporary place, as a guest article in a magazine
senses.definitionCN: 临时获得一席之地的事物，如杂志客座文章
senses.example: She wrote a guest post for our blog.
senses.exampleCN: 她为我们的博客写了一篇客座文章。
senses.why: Even ideas can knock on a door; temporary entries borrow the visitor image.
senses.whyCN: 连文章都能「敲门」做客，临时入驻借用访客的画面。

senses.title: One who is treated with care
senses.definition: anyone given special care and courtesy
senses.definitionCN: 受到特别款待与礼遇的人
senses.example: The team treats every customer as a guest of honor.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把每位顾客都当作贵宾对待。
senses.why: Once hosting is an attitude, anyone receiving it becomes a guest in spirit.
senses.whyCN: 当「款待」成为一种态度，任何被款待者都成了精神上的客人。

intro.en: Guest and host are an old pair; guest traveled through Old Norse into English.
intro.cn: guest 与 host 是一对古老的搭档；guest 经古诺斯语进入英语。

items.en: Proto-Germanic gastiz meant a stranger or guest, tied to ideas of hospitality.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 gastiz 意为陌生人、客人，与好客观念紧密相连。

items.en: Old English giest or gaest meant guest and also stranger.
items.cn: 古英语 giest / gaest 兼指客人与陌生人。

items.en: Old Norse gestr reinforced the word, giving the modern g-e-s-t shape.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gestr 强化了该词，形成现代的 g-e-s-t 词形。

items.en: Middle English gest settled as the everyday word for a visitor.
items.cn: 中古英语 gest 固定为「来访者」的日常用词。

items.en: Modern English extended it to hotel guests, show guests, and guest writers.
items.cn: 现代英语将其扩展到旅馆房客、节目嘉宾与客座作者。

note.cn: 与 guest 形近或义近的词。

examples.en: Every guest got a small gift at the wedding.

core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的门与一杯热茶

definition_zh: 引导；指导；导游；指南；指导手册
definition_en: to show someone the way or help them do something; a person or book that shows the way
core_image: 向导举着一面小旗走在最前面，队伍沿着他指的方向前进
scene: 博物馆里一位讲解员走在队伍最前面，每到一处展品就停下来讲解。The guide explained the history of every painting on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 guide 是「导游、讲解员」（第 3 个义项：带路并讲解的人）；句意是导游讲解了墙上每幅画的历史。

derivatives.zh: 由 guide 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「指导；引导」
由 guide + line 构成，义为「指导方针；准则」
由 mis-（错误地）+ guide 构成，义为「误导」

senses.title: To show the way
senses.definition: to lead a person or animal along a route
senses.definitionCN: 带领人或动物沿某条路线前进
senses.example: She guided the visitors to the exit.
senses.exampleCN: 她把参观者引到出口。
senses.why: The flag holder walks first, so the verb begins as physically leading the road.
senses.whyCN: 画面是举旗的人走在最前，动词最初就是实实在在的带路。

senses.title: To help control movement
senses.definition: to help something move in the right direction
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某物沿正确方向移动
senses.example: He guided the car into the narrow space.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车缓缓开进狭窄的车位。
senses.why: Hands on a wheel guide as much as feet on a path; direction-keeping is the shared idea.
senses.whyCN: 握方向盘与走路线同属「保持方向」，画面从脚步扩展到操控。

senses.title: A person who leads visitors
senses.definition: someone whose job is to show visitors around a place
senses.definitionCN: 以带游客参观为职业的人
senses.example: Our guide spoke three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的导游会说三种语言。
senses.why: The one who walks ahead gets a name, turning the action into a job title.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的人获得称呼，动作变成职业名。

senses.title: A book of instructions
senses.definition: a book or document that explains how to do or understand something
senses.definitionCN: 讲解如何做事或理解某物的书册
senses.example: Read the user guide before starting the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 开机前先读用户手册。
senses.why: A silent book can lead too; pages replace the walking leader.
senses.whyCN: 书也能带路，纸页代替了走在前面的人。

senses.title: Something that shapes decisions
senses.definition: a rule, feeling, or example that influences choices
senses.definitionCN: 影响决策的规则、感觉或榜样
senses.example: Her honesty is a guide for the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诚实是全班学习的榜样。
senses.why: Direction can be moral; the inner compass extends the leading image to choices.
senses.whyCN: 方向感也可以是道德的，内心指南针把「带路」延伸到抉择。

intro.en: Guide comes through French from a Germanic word about watching and showing the road.
intro.cn: guide 经古法语来自日耳曼语词，与「看路、指路」有关。

items.en: A Frankish root witan meant to show the way, related to words for watching.
items.cn: 法兰克语词根 witan 意为指路，与「看」类词相关。

items.en: Old French guider meant to lead or guide, borrowing the Germanic root.
items.cn: 古法语 guider 意为引导、带路，借自日耳曼词根。

items.en: Occitan forms helped carry the word across into northern French before English met it.
items.cn: 奥克语形式帮助该词传入北部法语，随后与英语相遇。（存疑关联）

items.en: Middle English borrowed gide or guide in the fourteenth century for both leading and advising.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 guide，兼指带路与劝导。

items.en: Modern English added guidebooks, user guides, and the moral sense of a guiding principle.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了指南书、用户手册以及「指导原则」的道德义。

entries.definitionCN: 行会；同业公会；与 guide 词形相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to move smoothly and continuously
entries.definitionCN: 滑行；与 guide 形近，词源无关

entries.definition: help and advice about how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 指导；引导，guide 的派生名词

entries.definition: to go in front and show the way
entries.definitionCN: 带领；走在前面

entries.definition: to tell someone how to get somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 指引；指挥

entries.definition: to go with someone to protect or guide them
entries.definitionCN: 陪同；护卫

abstract.cn: 手电光一节一节照亮前路。

abstract.en: a compass needle holding steady north

examples.en: The signposts will guide you to the beach.

examples.en: A good guide makes history come alive.
examples.cn: 好导游能让历史活起来。

examples.en: Parents guide children not by commands but by examples.
examples.cn: 父母以身作则而非命令来引导孩子。

definition_zh: 有罪的；内疚的；感到愧疚的
definition_en: responsible for breaking a law or doing something wrong; feeling shame about it
core_image: 低着头的孩子，双手绞在身后，明知自己做错了事
scene: 打碎了花瓶的孩子站在客厅角落，头埋得很低不敢看妈妈。The boy felt guilty about breaking his mother's favorite vase.
sceneCN: 这里 guilty 是「内疚的、愧疚的」（第 2 个义项：心里感到有错）；句意是男孩打碎妈妈心爱的花瓶后深感内疚。

derivatives.zh: 由 guilty 去掉 -y 构成，义为「罪行；内疚」
由 guilty 加 -ly 构成，义为「内疚地；心虚地」

senses.title: Responsible for a crime
senses.definition: shown by law to have done something illegal
senses.definitionCN: 经法律认定做了违法之事
senses.example: The court found him guilty of theft.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判定他犯有盗窃罪。
senses.why: The head-bowed picture first belongs to the courtroom, where guilt is proven.
senses.whyCN: 低头认错的画面首先出现在法庭，那里有罪与否由证据裁定。

senses.title: Feeling shame inside
senses.definition: feeling unhappy because you have done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因做错事而心里难受
senses.example: She felt guilty about lying to her friend.
senses.exampleCN: 她因对朋友撒谎而内疚。
senses.why: Not all wrongs reach a court; the same bowed head appears inside the heart.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有错事都会上法庭，同样低垂的头也会出现在心里。

senses.title: Looking or sounding ashamed
senses.definition: showing guilt through face, voice, or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 通过表情、声音或行为流露愧疚
senses.example: He gave a guilty smile when the teacher asked.
senses.exampleCN: 老师一问，他露出了心虚的笑。
senses.why: Inner shame leaks outward; the feeling paints itself on the face.
senses.whyCN: 内心的愧疚会外泄，情绪自己画在脸上。

senses.title: Deserving blame for a small fault
senses.definition: responsible for a mistake or carelessness, not a crime
senses.definitionCN: 对错误或疏忽负有责任（非罪行）
senses.example: Who is guilty of leaving the window open?
senses.exampleCN: 是谁没关窗户？
senses.why: Blame scales down; the courtroom word shrinks to fit everyday faults.
senses.whyCN: 责备可大可小，法庭用语缩小后用来指日常过失。

senses.title: Enjoyed with mild shame
senses.definition: used to describe a pleasure one feels slightly bad about
senses.definitionCN: 形容明知不太好却仍然享受的事物
senses.example: Chocolate cake is my guilty pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 巧克力蛋糕是我的罪恶快感。
senses.why: Enjoyment and shame can share one bite; the odd pair creates a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 享乐与愧疚可以咬在同一口里，奇特的组合固定成短语。

intro.en: Guilty grows from an old English word about debt and wrong payment.
intro.cn: guilty 源自一个关于「欠债、亏欠」的古英语词。

items.en: Old English gylt meant fault, sin, or even a payment due for a wrong.
items.cn: 古英语 gylt 意为过错、罪，甚至指因过错而应付的款项。

items.en: The adjective gyltig meant guilty or owing, joining the noun with -ig.
items.cn: 加 -ig 构成形容词 gyltig，意为有罪的、亏欠的。

items.en: Middle English guilty kept both the legal and the moral meanings.
items.cn: 中古英语 guilty 保留法律义与道德义。

items.en: Modern English fixed the court phrase plead guilty and the feeling phrase feel guilty.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 plead guilty（认罪）与 feel guilty（感到内疚）。

items.en: The playful phrase guilty pleasure appeared in recent centuries.
items.cn: guilty pleasure（罪恶快感）这一俏皮说法是近几个世纪出现的。

note.en: Words near guilty in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guilty 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: an association of workers
entries.definitionCN: 行会；与 guilty 词形相近，词源无关

entries.definition: the fact or feeling of having done wrong
entries.definitionCN: 罪行；内疚，guilty 的名词形式

entries.definition: covered with a thin layer of gold
entries.definitionCN: 镀金的；与 guilt 同音异义

entries.definition: feeling shame about something done
entries.definitionCN: 羞愧的，强调丢脸感

entries.definition: deserving blame
entries.definitionCN: 该受责备的

entries.definition: not guilty of a crime or fault
entries.definitionCN: 无罪的；清白的，guilty 的反义

normal.cn: guilt + y：词尾 y 把内疚画在脸上。

normal.en: feel guilty about + the wrong thing

normal.en: guilty pleasure is a phrase worth memorizing whole
normal.cn: guilty pleasure 值得整条背下来。

abstract.en: a child hiding a broken vase behind his back
abstract.cn: 孩子把打碎的花瓶藏到身后。

abstract.en: eyes sliding sideways during a question
abstract.cn: 被提问时眼珠偷偷往旁边溜。

abstract.en: a courtroom hammer paused mid-air
abstract.cn: 法槌悬在半空，等待判决。

examples.en: The jury declared the man not guilty.
examples.cn: 陪审团宣布该男子无罪。

examples.en: I always feel guilty when I skip my homework.
examples.cn: 一不写作业我就感到内疚。

examples.en: Her guilty expression gave the secret away.
examples.cn: 她心虚的表情泄露了秘密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给提」——做错事的人低着头等着被「给提」起来批评，guilty 就是心虚。

root: 源自古英语 gylt（过错、罪、应付的款项），加形容词后缀 -ig 构成 gyltig；词义从「亏欠」延伸到「有罪」，核心画面是「欠下一笔还不清的错」。

sensesIntro.en: From court conviction the word moves inward to shame, outward to looks, sideways to small faults, and playfully to pleasures.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭定罪走向内心羞愧，外显为神情，缩小到日常过失，最后俏皮地用于享乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowed head and hands behind the back
core.cn: 核心意象：低垂的头与背在身后的手

latinIntro.cn: 与 guilt 词族搭配的拉丁语系词。

items.example: A guilty look spread over her face.

items.example: Nothing feels guiltier than a lost promise.

items.example: The guiltiest moment came at midnight.

items.example: The judge set the innocent free.

items.example: The crime was caught on video.

definition_zh: 吉他；六弦琴
definition_en: a musical instrument with strings that you play with the fingers or a pick
core_image: 一把木质吉他斜抱在胸前，手指拨动琴弦，音符飞出
scene: 音乐教室里，老师把一把亮棕色的大琴抱到胸前，指尖在弦上一扫。The student practiced the guitar every evening after school.
sceneCN: 这里 guitar 是「吉他」（第 1 个义项：弦乐器本身）；句意是学生每天放学后练习吉他。

derivatives.zh: 由 guitar 加 -ist 构成，义为「吉他手；吉他演奏者」
由 guitar 加 -like 构成，义为「像吉他的」

senses.title: The string instrument itself
senses.definition: a hollow wooden instrument with usually six strings
senses.definitionCN: 通常有六根弦的木制空心乐器
senses.example: He bought a new guitar for the band.
senses.exampleCN: 他为乐队买了一把新吉他。
senses.why: The picture is the instrument held against the chest, so the first sense names the object.
senses.whyCN: 画面是抱在胸前的乐器本身，第一个义项就是这件物品。

senses.title: The part or sound of it
senses.definition: the guitar sounds in a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲中的吉他声部或音色
senses.example: Turn up the guitar in the mix.
senses.exampleCN: 把混音里的吉他调响一点。
senses.why: Once the object is named, its voice can be named after it in recordings.
senses.whyCN: 乐器被命名后，它在录音中的声音也以它命名。

senses.title: Playing it as a skill
senses.definition: the skill or activity of playing the guitar
senses.definitionCN: 弹奏吉他这门技能或活动
senses.example: She studies guitar at the music school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐学校学吉他。
senses.why: Objects become subjects; holding the guitar grows into studying it.
senses.whyCN: 物品可以变成学科，抱着吉他慢慢就变成学吉他。

intro.en: Guitar traveled a long southern road from ancient string instruments into English.
intro.cn: guitar 从古老的弦乐器出发，沿南方长路进入英语。

items.en: Ancient Greek kithara was a professional lyre-like string instrument.
items.cn: 古希腊语 kithara 是一种类似里拉的专业弦乐器。

items.en: Latin cithara borrowed the Greek word for string instruments.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cithara 借入了这个希腊语弦乐器名。

items.en: Old French and Spanish built guitare and guitarra for the flat-backed plucked instrument.
items.cn: 古法语与西班牙语据此造出 guitare / guitarra，指平背拨弦琴。

items.en: French guitare passed the word into English by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪前，法语 guitare 把这个词传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling guitar and later added electric guitars.
items.cn: 现代英语固定拼写 guitar，后来又有了电吉他。

note.en: Words near guitar in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guitar 形近或义近的词。

abstract.en: a pick flashing like a tiny coin

definition_zh: 枪；炮；喷射器；油枪；（动词）开枪；加大油门
definition_en: a weapon that fires bullets; a tool that sprays or shoots; to shoot or accelerate suddenly

senses.definition: a weapon that shoots bullets or shells
senses.definitionCN: 发射子弹或炮弹的武器
senses.example: Soldiers carry guns on duty.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵执勤时携带枪支。
senses.why: The first picture is the barrel and the trigger, a machine for releasing force at once.
senses.whyCN: 最初的画面是枪管与扳机，一台在一瞬间释放力量的机器。

senses.title: A tool that sprays
senses.definition: a device that pushes out liquid or glue with force

senses.title: To shoot with a gun

senses.title: A member of a shooting team or rank

senses.why: The tool stands for its best user, a common shift in English.

intro.en: Gun has a surprisingly personal origin story involving a famous name.
intro.cn: gun 的起源出人意料地与一个人名有关。

items.en: The medieval female name Gunhild or Gunilda was shortened to Gun for engines of war.
items.cn: 中世纪女名 Gunhild（贡希尔）被缩略为 Gun，用来称呼战争器械。

items.en: Fourteenth-century English records name siege engines Gunilda, and the nickname spread to cannon.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语文献把攻城器械命名为 Gunilda，昵称随后传给火炮。

items.en: Some scholars connect the name to Old Norse gunnr meaning war, though this is debated.
items.cn: 有学者把该名字与古诺斯语 gunnr（战争）相连，但尚有争议。

items.en: By the fifteenth century gun meant any firearm, large or small.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，gun 已泛指各种火器，大小皆可。

items.en: Modern English added spray guns, nail guns, and the verb of accelerating.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了喷枪、射钉枪以及「猛加速」的动词义。

senses.title: A group greeting

senses.example: Thanks, guys, for helping me move.

senses.title: To make fun of

intro.en: Gym hides a naked Greek secret at its root.
intro.cn: gym 的希腊语词根里藏着一个「赤身」的秘密。

items.en: Ancient Greek gumnazo meant to train, and gymnasts trained naked; gumnos meant naked.
items.cn: 古希腊语 gumnazo 意为训练，而训练者赤身进行；gumnos 意为裸体的。

items.en: Greek gymnasion was the training ground where young men exercised.
items.cn: 希腊语 gymnasion 是青年锻炼的训练场。

items.en: Latin borrowed gymnasion as gymnasium for training schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 gymnasion 作 gymnasium，指训练学校。

items.en: English took the full gymnasium in the seventeenth century, first for schools then sports halls.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入完整形式 gymnasium，先指学校后指运动馆。

items.en: The everyday shortening gym took over in speech and even in timetables.
items.cn: 口语缩略形式 gym 逐渐取代全称，连课表上也用它。

senses.title: A repeated personal action

senses.definitionCN: 反复多次以致自动化的行为

senses.title: A tendency of animals or plants

senses.example: Owls have nocturnal habits.

intro.en: Habit began as the idea of having or holding, then slid into what one wears and does.

items.en: Latin habere meant to have or hold, and habitus meant condition or state of holding oneself.

items.en: Habitus also named style of dress, the way one holds clothes on the body.
items.cn: habitus 也指穿着样式，即衣物在身上的持法。

items.en: Old French habit meant clothing and later general custom.
items.cn: 古法语 habit 指服装，后来泛指习俗。

items.en: Middle English habit first meant dress, especially of religious orders.
items.cn: 中古英语 habit 最初指衣着，尤指修会服饰。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the repeated-action meaning dominated English habit.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「反复行为」义在英语 habit 中占了主导。

examples.en: Brushing twice a day is a healthy habit.

root: 源自拉丁语 habere（拥有）的过去分词词干 habit-，habitus 指自身状态与穿着；经古法语 habit 进入中古英语时指修会服饰，后转为「惯常行为」，核心画面是「被反复握住的行为」。

sensesIntro.cn: 从「持有、穿着」落定到自动行为、动物习性、修士道袍、风俗与体质。

definition_zh: 头发；毛发；毛；（一点）少量
definition_en: the mass of thin threads that grows on the head or body of people and animals
core_image: 一把黑亮的头发从头顶垂下，梳子一滑到底
scene: 理发店里，理发师围好围布后拿起剪刀咔嚓作响。Grandma cut a long grey hair from her face.
sceneCN: 这里 hair 是「头发」（第 1 个义项：长在头上的细丝）；句意是奶奶把脸旁一根长长的白发剪掉了。

derivatives.zh: 由 hair 加 -y 构成，义为「多毛的；毛茸茸的」
由 hair + cut 构成，义为「理发；发型」
由 hair + -less 构成，义为「无毛的；秃的」

senses.title: Threads growing on the head
senses.definition: the mass of thin strands growing on the human head
senses.definitionCN: 长在人头上的成束细丝
senses.example: Her black hair shines in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 她的黑发在阳光下闪闪发亮。
senses.why: The first picture is the curtain of strands on the head, so the head sense leads.
senses.whyCN: 最先的画面是头顶垂下的细丝帘，头发义自然居首。

senses.title: A single strand
senses.definition: one thin thread of hair, countable
senses.definitionCN: 可数的一根细丝
senses.example: There is a hair in my soup.
senses.exampleCN: 我的汤里有一根头发。
senses.why: A curtain can be counted strand by strand when it falls alone.
senses.whyCN: 当细丝单独脱落时，帘子就能一根一根数。

senses.title: Fur on animals
senses.definition: the soft covering on the bodies of many animals
senses.definitionCN: 许多动物身上的柔软覆盖物
senses.example: The cat left hair on the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把毛留在了沙发上。
senses.why: People share the covering with animals, so the word stretches across species.
senses.whyCN: 人与动物共享这层覆盖物，词义顺势跨物种延伸。

senses.title: A tiny amount or distance
senses.definition: a very small distance or degree, as in win by a hair
senses.definitionCN: 极小的差距或程度，如 win by a hair
senses.example: The arrow missed by a hair.
senses.exampleCN: 箭差之毫厘。
senses.why: A single strand is nearly weightless, so it measures the smallest margins.
senses.whyCN: 一根发丝几乎没有重量，恰好用来丈量最小的差距。

senses.title: Hair as plant growth
senses.definition: fine thread-like parts on some plants or leaves
senses.definitionCN: 某些植物或叶片上的细丝状部分
senses.example: Peach skins carry soft hairs.
senses.exampleCN: 桃子表皮带着细细的茸毛。
senses.why: Nature reuses the thread shape, and the word follows the shape.
senses.whyCN: 自然界复用细丝形状，词义便随形状游走。

intro.en: Hair has a stubbornly old Germanic history with no Latin relatives.
intro.cn: hair 的日耳曼历史十分古老，且没有拉丁语亲戚。

items.en: A Germanic root harjas meant mane, bristles, or hair covering.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 harjas 意为鬃毛、鬃毛状覆盖物。

items.en: Old English her or hear meant hair of the head and of animals.
items.cn: 古英语 her / hear 兼指头发与动物毛。

items.en: No connection with Latin capillus or French cheveu exists; the root stands alone.
items.cn: 它与拉丁语 capillus、法语 cheveu 均无关联，词根独立存在。

items.en: Middle English heer kept both the mass and single-strand uses.
items.cn: 中古英语 heer 保留整体与单根两种用法。

items.en: Modern English spelled it hair and built dozens of compounds like haircut.
items.cn: 现代英语定形为 hair，并构成 haircut 等大量合成词。

note.en: Words near hair in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 hair 形近或义近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 马鬃；长鬃毛

normal.en: haircut, hairstyle, hairband are easy compounds

examples.cn: 理发师为夏天把我的头发剪短了。

examples.en: A grey hair appeared on his head.
examples.cn: 他头上冒出一根白头发。

examples.en: She tied her hair back before cooking.
examples.cn: 做饭前她把头发扎到脑后。

root: 源自日耳曼语词根 harjas（鬃毛、毛发），古英语作 her/hear，与拉丁语 capillus、法语 cheveu 无关；核心画面是「头顶垂下的细丝帘」。

sensesIntro.en: From the head curtain the word counts single strands, covers animal fur, measures tiny margins, and even names plant fuzz.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头顶发帘到可数的单根、动物毛皮、毫厘之差，乃至植物茸毛。

core.cn: 核心意象：黑细丝织成的帘子

intro.cn: hair 构词活跃，下面列出其词尾与最亲密伙伴。

latinIntro.cn: hair 没有拉丁语近亲，伙伴词来自英语与法语。

definition_zh: 一半；半个；（足球）半场；（副词）一半地
definition_en: one of two equal parts of something
core_image: 一块饼从正中切开，两半完全一样大
scene: 妈妈把刚出炉的披萨从正中切开，兄弟俩一人一半。Half of the pizza went to each brother.
sceneCN: 这里 half 是「一半」（第 1 个义项：二等分之一）；句意是半个披萨分给了每位兄弟。

derivatives.zh: 由 half + way 构成，义为「在中途；半路」
由 half + hearted 构成，义为「半心半意的；敷衍的」

senses.title: One of two equal parts
senses.definition: either of two equal parts into which something is divided
senses.definitionCN: 某物被平分成的两部分之一
senses.example: She ate half of the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她吃了蛋糕的一半。
senses.why: The picture is one clean cut, so the first sense is the equal share itself.
senses.whyCN: 画面是干脆的一刀，第一个义项就是平分后的那份。

senses.title: A part roughly dividing something
senses.definition: a part that divides something into two roughly equal pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把某物大致分成两半的部分
senses.example: Half the students agreed and half did not.
senses.exampleCN: 一半学生同意，一半不同意。
senses.why: Real cuts are rarely perfect, so half tolerates unequal shares.
senses.whyCN: 现实中难得切得完美，half 便容纳了不均的份。

senses.title: A sports period
senses.definition: one of two equal periods of a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛分成两个相等时段之一
senses.example: The team scored twice in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 该队上半场进了两球。
senses.why: A match is cut in two by time, exactly like the knife cuts the cake.
senses.whyCN: 比赛被时间一分为二，正如刀切蛋糕。

senses.title: A quantity less than whole
senses.definition: partly but not completely done or felt
senses.definitionCN: 部分地、未完全地完成或感受
senses.example: He gave a half smile and looked away.
senses.exampleCN: 他半笑了一下便移开目光。
senses.why: When the cut stays inside a feeling, only part of it shows.
senses.whyCN: 当切口落在情绪里，流露出来的只有一半。

senses.title: Half as a fraction number
senses.definition: the fraction one over two, written 1/2
senses.definitionCN: 数学中的二分之一分数
senses.example: Add half a cup of sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 加二分之一杯糖。
senses.why: Measuring needs exact parts, so the equal share becomes a number.
senses.whyCN: 计量需要精确的份额，平分的那份便化身为数字。

intro.en: Half keeps its oldest Germanic shape almost untouched for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: 一千多年来，half 几乎原封不动地保留着最古老的日耳曼词形。

items.en: Proto-Germanic halbaz meant one side of a divided thing.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 halbaz 意为被分之物的一侧。

items.en: Old English healf meant half but also a side or a part.
items.cn: 古英语 healf 意为一半，也指一侧、一部分。

items.en: Old Norse halfr reinforced the side meaning in northern texts.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 halfr 在北方文献中强化了「侧」的含义。

items.en: Middle English half widened into fractions, sports periods, and adverbs.
items.cn: 中古英语 half 扩展到分数、比赛半场与副词用法。

items.en: Modern English fixed the plural halves and compounds like halfway.
items.cn: 现代英语固定复数 halves 及 halfway 等合成词。

note.en: Words near half in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 half 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: to pull or lift with effort

entries.definition: a part served or divided out

entries.definition: twice as much
entries.definitionCN: 两倍，half 的反向概念

normal.cn: half of + 名词是最稳妥的表达式。

normal.en: halves and hives share the f-to-v spelling habit

abstract.en: two teams changing sides at the whistle

examples.en: Half the watermelon was gone in minutes.
examples.cn: 几分钟内半个西瓜就没了。

examples.en: The movie starts in half an hour.
examples.cn: 电影半小时后开场。

examples.en: They tied the game by the end of the second half.
examples.cn: 下半场结束时他们把比分扳平了。

sensesIntro.en: From the equal share the word moves to rough parts, sports halves, partial feelings, and exact fractions.

definition_zh: 在中途；到一半；半路； halfway house 过渡站
definition_en: at the middle point between two places or stages; partly done
core_image: 徒步者在两座山之间的歇脚亭里坐下，前不着村后不着店
scene: 长跑测试中，学生们绕操场跑到第二个弯道就到了半程点。We stopped halfway through the race for a drink of water.
sceneCN: 这里 halfway 是「在中途」（第 1 个义项：位于两地或两阶段的中点）；句意是赛跑进行到一半时我们停下喝水。

derivatives.zh: halfway 的基础词，义为「一半」
同族合成词，义为「半心半意的」

senses.title: At the middle of a route
senses.definition: at the point equally distant from the start and the end
senses.definitionCN: 位于起点与终点距离相等的那一点
senses.example: The bus stopped halfway up the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在半山腰停了下来。
senses.why: The rest shelter sits where effort equals remaining effort, the natural midpoint.
senses.whyCN: 歇脚亭所在之处，已走的路与将走的路恰好相等，这就是天然中点。

senses.title: At the middle of an activity
senses.definition: partly through an event, task, or period of time
senses.definitionCN: 活动、任务或时段进行了一部分
senses.example: Halfway through the film the power went out.
senses.exampleCN: 电影放到一半停电了。
senses.why: Any process is a road in disguise, so its middle borrows the travel word.
senses.whyCN: 一切过程都是变相的道路，其中点自然借用旅途词汇。

senses.title: Partly done or achieved
senses.definition: not finished; only partly complete
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完成；只完成了一部分
senses.example: The bridge is only halfway built.
senses.exampleCN: 大桥只建了一半。
senses.why: A stalled task stands frozen at its middle point, half a road behind it.
senses.whyCN: 搁浅的任务停在自己中点上，身后只有半条路。

senses.title: A compromise position
senses.definition: agreeing by each side giving up part of a demand
senses.definitionCN: 双方各让一步达成的中间立场
senses.example: Let us meet halfway on the price.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上我们各让一步吧。
senses.why: Two people walking toward each other meet at the middle, so deals use the same point.
senses.whyCN: 两人相向而行必在中点相遇，谈判也借用同一位置。

senses.title: Halfhearted or lukewarm
senses.definition: showing only partial effort, support, or warmth
senses.definitionCN: 只投入部分努力、支持或热情
senses.example: His halfway apology satisfied nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他不冷不热的道歉谁也不满意。
senses.why: A compromise spirit can shrink to a personality trait, lukewarm and unconvincing.
senses.whyCN: 折中的姿态缩小为性格特质，便成了温吞无力的敷衍。

intro.en: Halfway is simply half on a road, and its history mirrors the mother word.
intro.cn: halfway 就是「路上的半个」，历史与母词 half 如出一辙。

items.en: Old English healf carried the side-of-a-cut idea.
items.cn: 古英语 healf 承载「一刀之侧」的概念。

items.en: Old English weg meant road or way, a daily travel word.
items.cn: 古英语 weg 意为道路，是日常出行用词。

items.en: Middle English joined them as half way, first for physical midpoints.
items.cn: 中古英语把两词合并为 half way，最初指实际的中点。

items.en: The compound later stretched to time and progress midpoints.
items.cn: 合成词随后延伸到时间与进程的中点。

items.en: Modern English solidified the one-word spelling and the compromise senses.
items.cn: 现代英语固化了单词拼写与折中义项。

note.en: Words near halfway in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 halfway 形近或义近的词。

examples.en: The climbers rested halfway up the peak.

root: 由古英语 healf（一半）+ weg（道路）在中古英语合成，字面即「半路」；核心画面是「路程走到一半的那一点」。

sensesIntro.en: From a road midpoint the word spreads to task progress, unfinished work, compromises, and lukewarm effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 从道路中点延伸到任务进度、未竟之工、折中立场与敷衍态度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: equal road behind and ahead
core.cn: 核心意象：身后的路与前面的路一样长

intro.en: Halfway shows the half + noun pattern; the items below extend that pattern.
intro.cn: halfway 展示 half + 名词的构词法，下面延伸这一模式。

latinIntro.en: Germanic compounds with Latin conceptual partners.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼合成词与拉丁概念伙伴词。

items.example: Half the road is behind us.
We met midway through the park.
Stand in the middle of the line.
A halfhearted cheer rose from the bench.
items.exampleCN: 替补席传来稀落的欢呼。

items.example: The halfway point is at kilometer five.

definition_zh: 大厅；礼堂；走廊；门厅；（学生）宿舍食堂
definition_en: a large room or building for meetings, meals, or events; the area just inside a door
core_image: 推开大门先穿过一条铺着地毯的长走廊，尽头是灯光明亮的大厅
scene: 运动会颁奖礼在学校礼堂举行，全校师生坐得满满当当。The whole school gathered in the hall for the prize giving.
sceneCN: 这里 hall 是「礼堂」（第 2 个义项：举办集会活动的大厅）；句意是全校师生在礼堂参加颁奖典礼。

derivatives.zh: 由 hall + way 构成，义为「走廊；过道」
由 hall（金匠行会）+ mark 构成，义为「标志；特征」

senses.title: The space inside an entrance
senses.definition: the area or passage just inside the main door of a house
senses.definitionCN: 住宅大门内侧的区域或通道
senses.example: Leave your umbrella in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 把伞留在门厅里。
senses.why: A home's covered passage is its own little hall, the first hall people touch daily.
senses.whyCN: 住宅的遮盖通道就是人们每天最先触及的小 hall，门厅义由此而来。

senses.title: A large room for gatherings
senses.definition: a big room where many people meet, eat, or watch events
senses.definitionCN: 供许多人集会、用餐或观演的大房间
senses.example: The concert filled the hall with music.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会用音乐充满了大厅。
senses.why: When the passage grows into a giant room, it hosts crowds and becomes the grand hall.
senses.whyCN: 当通道放大成巨型房间，便能容纳人群，成为庄严的大厅。

senses.title: A large building or its owner
senses.definition: a big country house, or the family owning it, in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中的大宅，或拥有宅邸的家族
senses.example: The old hall stood beside the lake for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅在湖边立了三个世纪。
senses.why: The grandest roof in the village took the same name and lent it to the family.
senses.whyCN: 村里最气派的屋顶沿用此名，宅名又借给了家族。

senses.title: A college residence
senses.definition: a student residence or its common dining room at a college
senses.definitionCN: 大学的学生宿舍或其公共饭厅
senses.example: Freshmen live in hall for one year.
senses.exampleCN: 新生第一年住宿舍楼。
senses.why: Colleges feed students in one big room, so the meal hall names the whole residence.
senses.whyCN: 学院在同一个大房间里供餐，饭厅之名便指代整个宿舍。

senses.title: A workplace guild building
senses.definition: a building for a guild or city government, as in city hall
senses.definitionCN: 行会或市政机构的办公大厅，如 city hall
senses.example: Protesters gathered outside city hall.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者聚集在市政厅外。
senses.why: Public business once happened in one grand room, and the room named the institution.
senses.whyCN: 公务最初在一间大厅里办理，房间之名便转指机构本身。

intro.en: Hall is one of the oldest English words for a covered roof over people.
intro.cn: hall 是英语中最古老的「遮盖人群的屋顶」用词之一。

items.en: Old Norse holl meant a large house, a cognate that confirms the Germanic root.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 holl 意为大屋，同源词印证了日耳曼词根。

items.en: Proto-Germanic halla meant a covered place or rock shelter.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 halla 意为有遮盖之处或岩穴。

items.en: Old English heall meant the single big room where a chief's household lived and feasted.
items.cn: 古英语 heall 指首领家眷共同起居宴饮的那间大屋。

items.en: Middle English split the word into the house passage and the great gathering room.
items.cn: 中古英语把词分化为宅内通道与大型集会厅。

items.en: Modern English spread it to colleges, guilds, city government, and fame lists.
items.cn: 现代英语把它推广到学院、行会、市政与名人堂。

note.en: Words near hall in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 hall 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: one of two equal parts
entries.definitionCN: 一半；与 hall 一字母之差

entries.definition: frozen rain; to greet
entries.definitionCN: 冰雹；招呼；形近但词源无关

entries.definition: a passage inside a building
entries.definitionCN: 走廊，hall 的派生合成词

entries.definition: a long passage with doors on the sides
entries.definitionCN: 走廊，两侧带门的通道

entries.definition: a large room for audiences
entries.definitionCN: 礼堂；观众厅，侧重听演功能

entries.definition: the entrance room of a public building
entries.definitionCN: 大堂，公共建筑的门厅

normalIntro.cn: 五条 hall 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: dining hall is where students eat
normal.cn: dining hall（食堂）是学生用餐之处。

normal.en: hall and hall differ from half by one letter
normal.cn: hall 与 half 只差一个字母，书写小心。

normal.en: city hall means local government
normal.cn: city hall 代指地方政府，新闻高频词。

normal.en: hallway is the passage, hall the big room
normal.cn: hallway 是过道，hall 是大房间，对照记忆。

normal.en: hall of fame rewards the best
normal.cn: hall of fame（名人堂）表彰顶尖者。

abstract.en: a long carpet leading to bright doors
abstract.cn: 长地毯一直铺到亮灯的大门前。

abstract.en: a stage under a high ceiling
abstract.cn: 高天花板下的舞台。

abstract.en: rows of folded chairs waiting for a crowd
abstract.cn: 成排折叠椅静候人群。

examples.en: The birthday party was held in the school hall.
examples.cn: 生日会在学校礼堂举行。

examples.en: Her wet boots left prints in the hall.
examples.cn: 她的湿靴子在大厅留下脚印。

examples.en: Hundreds of students filled the dining hall at noon.
examples.cn: 中午数百名学生挤满食堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好」——大厅又高又亮，走进来一声「好」宽敞，hall 就是大厅。

root: 源自原始日耳曼语 halla（遮盖之处），古英语 heall 指首领宴居的大屋；与古诺斯语 holl 同源，核心画面是「屋顶下容纳众人的那一大间」。

sensesIntro.en: From a chief's feasting room the word reaches home passages, grand halls, mansions, colleges, and city government.
sensesIntro.cn: 从首领的宴饮大屋延伸到宅内通道、宏伟厅堂、大宅、学院与市政机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one great roof holding a crowd
core.cn: 核心意象：一片屋檐罩住众人

intro.en: Hall is ancient and short; the items below show its compounds and building neighbors.
intro.cn: hall 古老而短，下面列出其合成词与建筑近邻。

latinIntro.en: Latin building words that share hall's territory.
latinIntro.cn: 与 hall 领域重叠的拉丁语建筑词。

items.example: The hallway walls were freshly painted.
Kindness is the hallmark of the school.
items.exampleCN: 友善是这所学校的标志。

items.example: The dining hall opens at noon.
Meet me in the hotel lobby.
The guild met in its own hall.
items.exampleCN: 行会在自己的大厅集会。

items.example: The banquet filled the great hall.

definition_zh: 手；（钟表）指针；人手；帮助；（动词）递；交给
definition_en: the body part at the end of the arm; a worker; help; to pass something with the hand
core_image: 一只张开的手掌，能握笔能传球，五指灵活得像小工具
scene: 升旗仪式上，班长把崭新的校旗郑重交到旗手手中。Please hand your homework to the monitor after class.
sceneCN: 这里 hand 是动词「递交」（第 5 个义项：用手把东西交给别人）；句意是下课后把作业交给班长。

derivatives.zh: 由 hand + -ful 构成，义为「一把；少量」
由 hand 加 -y 构成，义为「便利的；手巧的」
由 hand + writing 构成，义为「笔迹；书写」

senses.title: The body part
senses.definition: the part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers and a thumb
senses.definitionCN: 手臂末端有手指与拇指的部位
senses.example: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 知道答案的请举手。
senses.why: The open palm is the original image, so the body part leads every other meaning.
senses.whyCN: 摊开的手掌是最初的画面，身体部位义统领其余义项。

senses.title: A pointer on a clock
senses.definition: the thin moving bar that shows hours or minutes on a clock
senses.definitionCN: 钟面上指示时分的细长条
senses.example: The minute hand moved slowly to twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 分针慢慢指向十二点。
senses.why: Early clock faces were pointed at by hand, so the pointer took the hand's name.
senses.whyCN: 早期钟面靠人手拨示时间，指针便借用了 hand 之名。

senses.title: A worker or crew member
senses.definition: a person employed to do physical work, as in farm hand
senses.definitionCN: 受雇做体力活的人，如 farm hand
senses.example: The ranch needed extra hands at harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场收获季需要额外人手。
senses.why: What a hand can do names who does it; the tool becomes the person.
senses.whyCN: 手能做的事代指做这件事的人，工具转指人。

senses.title: Help or applause
senses.definition: assistance given to someone, or clapping of hands
senses.definitionCN: 给予的协助，或拍手的喝彩
senses.example: Give me a hand with these boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 帮我搬一下这些箱子。
senses.why: Lending a hand literally offers the tool of work, so help wears the hand's name.
senses.whyCN: 借出一只手就是把劳动工具借出去，帮助于是以手为名。

senses.title: To pass or deliver
senses.definition: to put something into someone's hand or care
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放进他人手中或交由其保管
senses.example: Hand the tickets to the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 把票递给司机。
senses.why: Passing a thing ends in a palm; the verb captures the last inch of the journey.
senses.whyCN: 传递的终点是掌心，动词捕捉了这最后一寸旅程。

intro.en: Hand is a pure Germanic word, as old as English itself.
intro.cn: hand 是纯粹的日耳曼语词，与英语本身一样古老。

items.en: Proto-Germanic handuz named the grasping limb, related to words for taking.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 handuz 指抓握之肢，与「取」类词相关。

items.en: Old English hond meant the hand and, already, power or side, as in the left hand of an army.
items.cn: 古英语 hond 指手，且已引申出力量与「一侧」，如军队的左翼。

items.en: Middle English added the clock pointer, the worker, and the giving verb.
items.cn: 中古英语增加指针、人手与递交动词诸义。

items.en: Fixed phrases like on the other hand spread through debate and writing.
items.cn: on the other hand 等固定短语随论辩与书面语普及。

items.en: Modern English compounded hand into hundreds of tools and jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 hand 构成了数百个工具与职业合成词。

note.en: Words near hand in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 hand 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: useful and easy to reach or use
entries.definitionCN: 便利的；手巧的，hand 的派生词

entries.definition: a flat strip; a music group
entries.definitionCN: 带子；乐队；与 hand 一字母之差

entries.definition: at the back of the body
entries.definitionCN: 后面的（如后腿）；形近但词源不同

entries.definition: the inner surface of the hand
entries.definitionCN: 手掌心，hand 的局部

entries.definition: to give something to someone else
entries.definitionCN: 传递，与动词 hand 近义

entries.definition: one of the long parts of the hand
entries.definitionCN: 手指，hand 的组成部分

normalIntro.cn: 五条 hand 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: hand in hand means together side by side
normal.cn: hand in hand（手拉手）表示相伴同行。

normal.en: on the other hand introduces the opposite view
normal.cn: on the other hand 引出相反观点。

normal.en: give a hand is help and applause
normal.cn: give a hand 既是帮忙也是鼓掌。

normal.en: second hand once meant the small clock pointer
normal.cn: second hand 原指秒针，后转指二手。

normal.en: handful, handy, handwriting grow from one root
normal.cn: handful、handy、handwriting 同根生长。

abstract.en: five fingers closing around a pencil
abstract.cn: 五指合拢握住铅笔。

abstract.en: a red envelope passed palm to palm
abstract.cn: 红包从一只掌心递到另一只掌心。

abstract.en: a clock hand sweeping past noon
abstract.cn: 钟表指针扫过正午。

examples.en: Hand me that pencil, please.
examples.cn: 请把那支铅笔递给我。

examples.en: Every hand was raised in the classroom.
examples.cn: 教室里人人都举起了手。

examples.en: The clock has a bright red second hand.
examples.cn: 这只钟有一根鲜红的秒针。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「汗的」——干完活手心全是汗，hand 就是劳动的手。

root: 源自原始日耳曼语 handuz（抓握之肢），古英语 hond 兼指手与力量；核心画面是「能抓能握能传递的五指」。

sensesIntro.en: From the grasping limb the word reaches clock pointers, hired workers, help, applause, and the act of passing things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从抓握之肢延伸到钟表指针、雇工、帮助、掌声与递送动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm ready to hold or give
core.cn: 核心意象：随时可握可给的摊开手掌

intro.en: Hand builds words like no other body part; the items below sample the family.
intro.cn: hand 的构词力冠绝身体部位词，下面抽样其词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin manual words cover the same ground.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manual 系列覆盖同样的领域。

items.example: A handful of rice fed the bird.
This tool is handy in the kitchen.
She left her handbag on the chair.
items.exampleCN: 她把手提包忘在椅子上。

items.example: She snapped her fingers to the beat.

items.exampleCN: 竖大拇指是开心的手势。

definition_zh: 手提包；手袋；挎包
definition_en: a small bag carried in the hand or on the arm, holding personal things
core_image: 一只提在手腕上的方形小包，装着钥匙、钱包和口红
scene: 出门前妈妈站在穿衣镜前，把手机、钥匙一样样放进提包。She carried a leather handbag to the office party.
sceneCN: 这里 handbag 是「手提包」（第 1 个义项：手提收纳个人物品的袋）；句意是她拎着一只皮质手袋去参加公司聚会。

derivatives.zh: handbag 的基础词，义为「袋子」
美式对应说法，义为「手袋；钱包」

senses.title: A personal carry bag
senses.definition: a small bag holding money, keys, and personal items
senses.definitionCN: 装钱、钥匙与私人物品的小包
senses.example: Her handbag matched her shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手袋和鞋子很配套。
senses.why: The picture is a palm-sized container held in the hand, so the object itself leads.
senses.whyCN: 画面是握在手中的小容器，物件本身即为第一义项。

senses.title: The bag as a fashion item
senses.definition: a handbag chosen for style or brand, not just use
senses.definitionCN: 以款式或品牌为选择标准的手袋
senses.example: Designer handbags cost more than phones.
senses.exampleCN: 名牌手袋比手机还贵。
senses.why: Once an object is carried daily, fashion claims it and the price follows.
senses.whyCN: 日常随身之物被时尚收编，价格也随之攀升。

senses.title: The contents carried
senses.definition: the personal items inside the bag, as in search her handbag
senses.definitionCN: 包内的私人物品，如搜查手袋
senses.example: The guard checked each handbag at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 保安在门口逐一检查手袋。
senses.why: The container stands for what it holds, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 容器代指所装之物，英语常见此类转喻。

senses.title: A prize or status symbol
senses.definition: an expensive bag showing wealth or rank
senses.definitionCN: 展示财富或地位的名贵包
senses.example: In the film the villain judges everyone by their handbag.
senses.exampleCN: 电影里反派以手袋评判他人。
senses.why: Fashion value turns into social signal; the bag speaks before its owner does.
senses.whyCN: 时尚价值转化为社交信号，包先于主人开口说话。

intro.en: Handbag is a young compound, younger than the two words that build it.
intro.cn: handbag 是个年轻的合成词，比构成它的两个词都年轻。

items.en: Old English hand named the grasping limb.
items.cn: 古英语 hand 指抓握之肢。

items.en: Old Norse baggi gave English bag for a sack or pouch.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 baggi 给英语带来 bag，指袋、囊。

items.en: Middle English used bags for travel and money pouches.
items.cn: 中古英语用 bag 指旅行行囊与钱袋。

items.en: In the mid-nineteenth century handbag was coined for a bag carried in the hand.
items.cn: 十九世纪中叶人们造出 handbag 一词，指手提之袋。

items.en: Twentieth-century fashion turned the word into a luxury category.
items.cn: 二十世纪时尚业把该词变成奢侈品类目。

note.en: Words near handbag in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 handbag 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: rare playful use meaning swinging a handbag
entries.definitionCN: 戏谑用法，挥舞手袋（罕用）

entries.definition: a small bell rung by hand
entries.definitionCN: 手铃；同构词但意义无关

entries.definition: a small reference book held in the hand
entries.definitionCN: 手册；同前缀合成词，便于对照

entries.definition: a small bag for money, American sense
entries.definitionCN: （美式）手袋；钱包

entries.definition: a bag carried on the back
entries.definitionCN: 双肩包，背携方式不同

entries.definition: a flat case for money and cards
entries.definitionCN: 钱包，仅收纳钱证

normalIntro.cn: 五条 handbag 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: hand + bag literally a bag in the hand
normal.cn: hand + bag 字面就是「手里的袋」。

normal.en: British handbag equals American purse
normal.cn: 英式 handbag 对应美式 purse。

normal.en: designer handbag signals luxury
normal.cn: designer handbag（名牌手袋）是奢侈品信号。

normal.en: handbag joins a big hand-family of compounds
normal.cn: handbag 属庞大的 hand 合成词家族。

normal.en: carry, not wear, a handbag
normal.cn: 手袋用 carry 而非 wear，动词要选对。

abstract.en: a zipper smiling open over keys
abstract.cn: 拉链咧开露出钥匙。

abstract.en: a strap swinging from a bent elbow
abstract.cn: 提带从弯着的手肘荡下。

abstract.en: a queue of bags at an airport scanner
abstract.cn: 安检机上排队的小包。

examples.en: She keeps a small umbrella in her handbag.
examples.cn: 她手袋里常备一把小伞。

examples.en: The handbag on sale was half price.
examples.cn: 那只促销手袋半价出售。

examples.en: Please watch my handbag while I buy tickets.
examples.cn: 我去买票时请帮我看一下手提包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「憨袋」——憨憨的手一直拎着袋子，handbag 就是手提包。

root: 由古英语 hand（手）与古诺斯语 baggi（袋）在十九世纪合成，字面即「手提之袋」；核心画面是「挂在手腕上的私人小仓库」。

sensesIntro.en: From a simple carry bag the word rises into fashion, contents, and status.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的随身袋上升到时尚单品、袋中之物与身份象征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bag hanging from a hand
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在手上的小包

branches.cn: 提带与手腕相遇的一刻

intro.cn: handbag 是双部件合成词，下面拆解各部件与 bag 词族近邻。

latinIntro.en: Bag words come from the north, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: bag 系列词源自北方语言而非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 手袋在店墙上一字排开。

His wallet is thin but old.

items.exampleCN: 我的双肩包装了三本课本。
行李箱吱呀地滑过地砖。

definition_zh: 发生；出现；碰巧；偶然遇到
definition_en: to take place or occur, often without being planned
core_image: 天上突然掉下一滴雨，正好落在路人的鼻尖上
scene: 上美术课时窗外忽然乌云密布，一场大雨说来就来。What will happen if we forget our umbrellas?
sceneCN: 这里 happen 是「发生」（第 1 个义项：事情出现）；句意是如果我们忘带雨伞会发生什么呢。

derivatives.zh: 由 happen 加 -ing 构成，义为「发生的事情；事件」
由同根词 hap 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地；或许」（旧式）

senses.title: To take place
senses.definition: to occur, especially without being planned or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 出现、发生，尤指非计划或非可控之事
senses.example: A funny thing happened on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上发生了一件趣事。
senses.why: The raindrop lands where it will; events fall uninvited, so the verb means simply to occur.
senses.whyCN: 雨滴想落哪就落哪，事情不请自来，动词义就是「发生」。

senses.title: To do or be by chance
senses.definition: to have the chance fact of doing or being something
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而做了某事或处于某状态
senses.example: I happened to see her at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我碰巧在车站见到她。
senses.why: Chance can land on you as easily as rain; meeting by luck wears the same word.
senses.whyCN: 偶然像雨一样落在人身上，偶遇也套用同一个词。

senses.title: To come to someone's lot
senses.definition: to be experienced by someone, as in what happened to you
senses.definitionCN: 降临到某人身上，被某人经历
senses.example: Look what happened to my old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 看看我的旧自行车遭遇了什么。
senses.why: Events drop onto people from above, so the person becomes the landing spot.
senses.whyCN: 事件从天而降，人便成了落点。

senses.title: To exist as an event worth noting
senses.definition: to produce an event or excitement, as in nothing ever happens here
senses.definitionCN: 产生值得注意的事件或热闹，如这里从无事发生
senses.example: Nothing ever happens in this quiet town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座安静的小镇从无新闻。
senses.why: Where no drops fall, the ground stays dull; events are measured by their falling.
senses.whyCN: 没有雨滴落下，地面便沉闷；事件以「是否落下」来衡量。

intro.en: Happen grows from an old northern word for luck itself.
intro.cn: happen 从一个古老的北方词「运气」生长而来。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant good luck or chance, the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为好运、机缘，是整个词族的种子。

items.en: Old English borrowed gehap meaning fitness or convenience.
items.cn: 古英语借入 gehap，意为适宜、便利。

items.en: Middle English hap meant luck, both good and bad.
items.cn: 中古英语 hap 意为运气，好坏皆可。

items.en: The verb happen was formed from hap with the -en ending, first meaning to come by chance.
items.cn: 由 hap 加 -en 构成动词 happen，最初意为偶然降临。

items.en: Modern English generalized it to any occurrence and kept happy, perhaps, mishap in the family.
items.cn: 现代英语泛化其义为任何事件，同族的 happy、perhaps、mishap 保留至今。

note.en: Words near happen in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 happen 形近或义近的词。

definition_zh: 快乐的；幸福的；满意的；乐意的； Lucky 的（巧的是）
definition_en: feeling or showing pleasure; satisfied; willing
core_image: 嘴角上扬到眼睛里，整张脸像被阳光点亮
scene: 收到录取通知的那一刻，她抱着信封在院子里转圈大笑。The children were happy to see fresh snow in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 happy 是「高兴的、快乐的」（第 1 个义项：感到愉悦）；句意是孩子们看到清晨的新雪非常开心。

pos.zh: 快乐的；幸福的；满意的；乐意的

derivatives.zh: 由 happy 变 y 为 i 加 -ness 构成，义为「幸福；快乐」
由 happy 变 y 为 i 加 -ly 构成，义为「快乐地；幸运地」

senses.title: Feeling pleasure
senses.definition: feeling or showing pleasure or delight
senses.definitionCN: 感到或表现出愉悦
senses.example: She gave a happy jump at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到消息她开心地跳了起来。
senses.why: Luck landing on you lights the face; the smile is the visible drop of good hap.
senses.whyCN: 好运落在身上点亮了脸，笑容就是那滴好运的可见形态。

senses.title: Satisfied with something
senses.definition: satisfied or contented with what one has
senses.definitionCN: 对已有之物感到满足
senses.example: Are you happy with your new desk?
senses.exampleCN: 你对新桌子满意吗？
senses.why: Good luck is not only big joy; quiet contentment counts as a lucky state too.
senses.whyCN: 好运不一定是狂喜，平静的满足同样是幸运的状态。

senses.title: Willing to do something
senses.definition: glad and willing to do or give something
senses.definitionCN: 乐于做某事或给予某物
senses.example: We are happy to answer your questions.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乐于回答您的问题。
senses.why: A generous mood offers itself freely, like luck given without asking.
senses.whyCN: 慷慨的心境主动奉上，恰似不求自来的好运。

senses.title: Lucky or suitable by chance
senses.definition: brought by chance and welcome, as in a happy coincidence
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然且受欢迎的，如 happy coincidence
senses.example: A happy accident gave the painting its glow.
senses.exampleCN: 一次幸运的意外让这幅画有了光泽。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives here; good hap is preserved in lucky accidents.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项在这里存续，好运保存在幸运的意外中。

senses.title: Apt or well chosen
senses.definition: suitable and well chosen, as in a happy phrase
senses.definitionCN: 合适且选用得当，如贴切的措辞
senses.example: She found a happy word for the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这首诗找到了一个贴切的词。
senses.why: When chance meets skill, the result fits perfectly, like a lucky catch.
senses.whyCN: 偶然遇上技巧，结果恰到好处，如同一次幸运的接球。

intro.en: Happy literally means having luck, and time has turned luck into joy.
intro.cn: happy 的字面义是「有好运的」，时间把好运酿成了快乐。

items.en: Old Norse happ meant good luck or good chance.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 happ 意为好运、良机。

items.en: Middle English hap meant fortune, good or bad.
items.cn: 中古英语 hap 意为运气，好坏兼指。

items.en: The adjective happy first meant lucky, as in a happy chance.
items.cn: 形容词 happy 最初意为幸运的，如 happy chance。

items.en: By the fifteenth century it meant glad and contented more often than lucky.
items.cn: 到十五世纪它更多表示快乐、满足而非幸运。

items.en: Modern English kept the lucky flavor in happy coincidence and fixed phrases like happy hour.
items.cn: 现代英语在 happy coincidence、happy hour 等短语中保留了幸运的余味。

note.en: Words near happy in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 happy 形近或义近的词。
